items.title: What's new on the wall
items.line: After an update, the next person who walks up to a tablet sees a short list of what is new, with a small picture for each.
items.more: Tap a line to read more, or "Show me" to open it or light up its card. "Got it" closes it, or it fades by itself after a minute and comes back once. It shows once on each screen, never in guest mode, over the screensaver, the doorbell or a call. A new tablet does not show it. In the studio, ⋯ then "What's new…" lists the same, with the studio's own changes too.

items.title: Swipe between menu pages
items.line: When a page is open from the side menu, swipe left or right to go to the next or the previous one, in the menu's order.
items.more: Small dots at the bottom show where you are. A swipe never starts on a button, a light tile, a slider or the thermostat dial, so it never changes anything in the house.

fixed: Drive time now finds the places in your calendar.
Talk at the front door: your voice now reaches the Eufy doorbell, and you hear the visitor on the tablet.

items.title: A fuller weather and calendar in the Cards screensaver
items.line: The weather now fills the screen with the sky outside right now, which changes with the time of day and the weather.
items.more: It shows one plain sentence about what comes next, such as "Dry until 6 PM, then rain", the coming hours with a soft temperature curve and rain bars, and the next three days. Small tiles with their glance pictures, such as the wind compass and the humidity ring, show feels like, wind, UV, sunrise or sunset and humidity only when they matter, such as strong wind or a high UV level. To keep them on, tick "Always show weather details" in the studio, under Screensaver, and pick up to five tiles and their order. The calendar shows your day: the date, the next event with how long until it starts, today's events on a time line with the weather for each hour, and a short look at tomorrow.

items.title: Make the weather's full view your own
items.line: In the studio, open the weather card or the Weather button and choose "Its full view".
items.more: Turn parts on or off, such as the story, the small tiles, the next 24 hours, the 7-day forecast and the radar, and move them up or down. Pick up to six small tiles and their order, now also with feels like and sunrise or sunset. The screensaver's weather uses the same tiles, so you set them once. On the wall, press and hold a part of the view to move it or hide it, with no studio needed. It is the same on every screen. Other full views follow in the next releases.

items.title: Arrange a screen on the wall itself
items.line: Hold the clock for 3 seconds and tap "Arrange this screen".
items.more: Tap a card, then tap the card it should trade places with. Use + and − to make a card larger or smaller, and the eye to hide it. A hidden card keeps its settings and comes back with one tap on "Show", on the wall or in the studio ("Show this card": Hidden). "Add a card" offers the few cards that fit that room, such as its lights, its music, a timer or the weather, each already set to the right device: one tap, no forms. Cameras, locks, the alarm and the garage are still added only in the studio. Undo is always one tap away. Only that screen changes, and only where its cards sit, their size and whether they show. To lock it, turn off "Allow changes on the wall" in the studio under Look. Guest mode always turns it off.

items.title: Guest phone remote
items.line: In guest mode, the welcome card has a second code.
items.more: A babysitter or guest scans it, and their phone becomes a small remote for the lights, scenes, music, shades and thermostat, with no app and no login. It never reaches the locks, alarm, cameras or garage. The link works only while guest mode is on, ends with it, and you can end it at any time. Add "Who to call" in the studio, and the sitter gets call buttons on the wall and on the phone. You can also copy the link in the studio and send it ahead.

items.title: Care for family homes
items.line: A calm view of a family member's home on your wall, such as your parents' home.
items.more: The Care card shows when their day started, a soft line of the day, and "Out" or "Resting" when that is normal. A gentle line comes on every wall when a normal day does not happen: a quiet morning, a long quiet day, a cold or very warm home, or a home that does not answer. If nobody touches it, your phones get one quiet note 10 minutes later, never at night. Their home learns its own normal from its history, with no new sensors and no monthly fee. Only the shape of the day is shared, never rooms, cameras or names, and one touch on their wall makes it private until tomorrow. Send a heart from the card, and they can send one back. Sharing a home is free; watching one is Pro. Both homes need Dashboard Studio: set it up in the studio under Family homes.

items.title: Room presence
items.line: Each wall tablet now tells Home Assistant when someone is in its room.
items.more: You get one sensor for each room with a tablet, such as "Kitchen presence", joined with the motion sensors you already have. With wall app 0.5.22, the tablet also notices someone who sits still and reads, so the room does not turn "empty" after two minutes. Only a number leaves the tablet, never a picture. The Living picture, Room to room and your own automations use it. Turn it off in the studio under Look, "Room presence".

items.title: Habits, the home that learns you
items.line: Every night Home Assistant looks at its own last three weeks, on your own machine, for what you do by hand again and again, such as the same lights off at about 11 PM most nights, the porch light a little after sunset, or the hall light right after the garage opens in the dark.
items.more: Add the new Habits card, and it offers one idea at a time in one plain sentence, with how often it happened and what it would change. Tap "Yes, do it", and the home does it from then on, with no automation to write. Lights go off softly and not while someone is still in the room, lights come on only when someone is home, and Undo stays after each run. If you change it back twice, the habit pauses itself and tells you. It never copies an automation you already have, and it never unlocks a door or opens the garage. The studio lists every habit under Home moments, with Pause and Stop.

items.title: "Where is everyone?" and "Is anyone in the kitchen?"
items.line: Ask any tablet, and it says who is in which room, in English, French, German and Spanish.

items.title: A smaller wall app
items.line: Wall app 0.5.22 is about 15 MB instead of 39 MB, so tablets update faster.
items.more: Hand gestures (Pro) now get their hand model once, from your own Home Assistant, the first time they turn on.

items.title: A "Hand gestures" switch
items.line: In the studio, under a TV's "Listen with" tablet, turn off hand gestures for that tablet.
items.more: Its voice keeps working.

items.title: Energy this week, with no energy meter
items.line: Home Assistant already knows when each light, TV, heater, fan or plug was on, so it now guesses what each one used.
items.more: Add the new "Energy this week" card. It shows one plain tip a week, such as "The Office lights were on for 31 hours while nobody was home. Turning them off when you leave saves about $3 a month." A soft ribbon under it shows where the energy goes, with the tip's own part lit. Tap the card to see what used the most, with no numbers. A plug that measures its own energy is counted as measured. The price comes from your Energy settings, or a typical price for your country. Every number says "about", because it is a guess. The Energy card uses it too when there is no meter. Ask "How much energy did we use this week?" and the assistant answers from it.

items.title: Live intercom
items.line: Say "call the kitchen", or tap a room on the new Intercom card.
items.more: The kitchen tablet knocks and shows who is calling. Just talk to answer: nothing leaves the kitchen until someone there speaks. If nobody answers, you can leave a voice message right away. Say "hang up" or tap End. "Call" on a voice message calls back.

items.title: Talk at the front door
items.line: When the doorbell rings, tap Talk and your voice comes out of the doorbell, from any tablet.
items.more: Quick replies say "Please leave it at the door" and more in your home's voice with one tap. Say "answer the door" to start. It uses the Eufy Security add-on you already have.

items.title: A first wow on the wall
items.line: When a new wall tablet has picked its room, it plays a short hello of about 20 seconds with your own home: rain on the glass, snow, a welcome home and the front door, with one calm line for each.
items.more: A touch ends it. It plays once on each tablet.

items.title: "Now put it on a wall"
items.line: The last step of a new setup now shows a code that opens the free wall app on an Android or Fire tablet.
items.more: "Phone or browser" shows the plain address, as before.

items.title: An empty home sees what it will get
items.line: When Home Assistant has no rooms or devices yet, the studio offers our demo home, built the same way your own first screen will be.
items.more: Your login stays, and "Back to my home" returns.

items.title: The trial shows the Pro moments
items.line: A new home's first screen now starts its 14-day trial with Weather on the glass, Welcome home and the night path turned on, each marked "Trial" in the studio.
items.more: Three days before the end, the studio says which moments will rest. On the last evening, a wall tablet plays back what it did during the trial, such as the days it rained. When the trial ends, these Pro moments rest on the tablets, and everything else stays. On a free plan, Pro moments that were turned on before now rest too.

items.title: Ask for help by voice
items.line: Say "Okay Nabu, I have an idea" or "report a problem" to any wall tablet, then just talk.
items.more: The tablet writes it down. While you talk, tap the card you mean, and it gets a ring. Then the screen shows exactly what would be sent: your words, the kind of tablet, the look and the kinds of cards. Turn on "Add a picture of this screen" if you like: cameras, photos and people are hidden, and you can hide all words too. Say "yes" or tap Send, and it goes to us, the makers. When your idea ships, the tablet tells you: "Your idea from 27 Nov is here, in version 1.4.180." You can also start it from the Assist page. A real picture needs the next wall apps; until then the tablet sends a drawing of its cards.

items.title: The weather card says when the rain or snow stops, when it has room
items.line: "Raining now, stops around 4 PM", or "Rain from 7 AM tomorrow, stops around 3 PM".
items.more: A short break of one dry hour does not count as a stop. On a small card it says "Rain until 4 PM".

items.title: Drive time
items.line: Add the new "Drive time" card, or keep your Smart card.
items.more: In the hour before you need to leave, it says "Leave by 5:40 PM for Angela's dentist" with "22 min, traffic is light", for the next calendar event that has a place. It says the traffic in words, and when it is heavy it says how much longer than usual. If snow or rain is forecast at the leaving time, it says to leave a few minutes early. A soft road fills as the time comes, and the car glows at the time to leave. The rest of the day it is quiet. Give it your work place and the time to be there, and on work days it shows the drive to work in the morning too. Online meetings are skipped. The drive times come from Waze, free, through Home Assistant: no account, no key and no new device.

items.title: The wall hears alarms
items.line: A wall tablet that may use its microphone now also listens for the beep pattern of a smoke alarm or a carbon monoxide alarm, even an old one that is not smart.
items.more: When it hears two full rounds of the pattern, every tablet shows the emergency for that room, your phones are told, and the lights come on, the same as with a smoke sensor. When the beeping stops, the tablets say so. A smoke alarm that chirps for a new battery becomes one calm line in the day instead. Only the word "smoke" or "CO" leaves the tablet, never sound. It works on the iPad app and browsers that listen for the wake word now, and on Android and Fire tablets with wall app 0.5.22. Turn it off in the studio under Home moments, Emergencies.

items.title: Sunrise before a wake-up alarm
items.line: For 20 minutes before an alarm you set by voice, the lights in that tablet's room grow from a faint warm glow to daylight, and the resting screen shows the sky before sunrise, brightening with them.
items.more: Lights that are already on are left alone, and a light you turn off stays off. Turn it off in the studio under Home moments.

items.title: Cheaper power hours
items.line: Home Assistant now knows when power costs less today, with no meter and no account.
items.more: In Ontario it follows the fixed time-of-use clock (or ultra-low overnight, if you pick it in the studio), with weekends and holidays. Elsewhere it uses a price sensor such as Nord Pool. The Energy this week card shows the next 24 hours as a soft band with the cheap hours lit, and one line such as "Cheaper power from 7 PM." When cheap power starts within the hour and the dishwasher, washer or dryer is waiting, the nearest screen says "Cheaper power in 40 minutes. Start the dishwasher then." No prices are shown, only cheap or not. Pick the plan in the studio under Home moments.

items.title: Kitchen helper
items.line: Share a recipe page from your phone to the Home Assistant app, as you share a YouTube video.
items.more: The kitchen tablet opens it in large letters: first the ingredients, then one step at a time. Say "next", "back", "repeat" or "ingredients", wave your hand, or touch the step to move on. A step such as "bake for 35 minutes" starts its own timer when it shows. It works with almost every recipe site, with no account and no AI. Type a screen's name in the share box to send it somewhere else.

items.title: Your own list on Today
items.line: When the screen knows who is in front of it (Follow me, or the only one at home), the Today card shows the first thing on their own to-do list, such as "Call the dentist, and 1 more".
items.more: A list named after the person ("Angela's list") counts as theirs.

items.title: Family window
items.line: Live video between your wall and a family home you watch with Care for family homes.
items.more: Touch the camera button next to their home on the Care card, or say "call Mom". Their wall shows you at the window, without sound, and sends nothing until someone there touches Open. They can open a window to you too. It uses the tablets' own cameras and the Care link: no account, no phone number, no new device. Pictures are small (a window, not a film). Wall tablets need wall app 0.5.22 for the camera; an iPad or a tablet without it sends sound only for now.

items.title: Open anything by voice
items.line: Say "open Media", "show me the family", "go to the cameras" or "open the kitchen", and the screen you talk to opens it, as a tap would.
items.more: It works for every side menu button, every card that opens a page, and the rooms, by the names the screen shows, in English, French, German and Spanish. Say "close" or "go back" to close it. "Open the garage door" still opens the garage door.

items.title: A pin on more pages
items.line: Timers, Stopwatch, Weather, Calendar, To-do lists and Family now have the pin that Media and News had.
items.more: A pinned page stays open and the screensaver waits. While a timer, the stopwatch or music runs, it also keeps the screen on, and it lets go five minutes after that ends. Say "pin this", "keep it open" or "pin the timer" (Pro), and "unpin" to let it close again.

items.title: The line of light around the screen while a timer runs now has a small tab at the top with the time left, so it reads as a timer
items.line: Tap it to open the timers.

fixed: "Time is up" could show without a sound when the tablet had rested during the timer.
The iPad and browsers no longer wake from a TV playing nearby.
The Russian wake words are stricter while a TV plays, so Russian speech on TV no longer starts them.
Eufy cameras: fewer wake-ups and a quieter log.

items.title: Magic setup
items.line: A new tablet or TV with the wall app asks which room it is in.
items.more: Tap the room, and its screen builds itself from what is in that room. The kitchen gets a timer, the entrance gets the doors and the door camera, and the bedroom goes dark at night.

items.title: Room to room
items.line: A video, a camera or music comes with you when you walk into another room.
items.more: The screen there goes on at the same moment, and the old one shows "Bring back". Say "follow me" or "bring it here" to move it at once. Choose "By itself", "Ask first" or "Off" in the studio.

items.title: Louder by voice follows the music
items.line: Say "louder", "quieter" or "volume 30" to a tablet, and the speaker that plays in that room changes, such as the kitchen Bose.
items.more: Speakers that play together change together. When nothing plays there, the TV changes, as before. A thumb up or down works the same way.

items.title: Home replay
items.line: Ask "What happened today?" and the wall plays your day as a short film of about 30 seconds.
items.more: It tells who came and went, each doorbell ring and parcel with its picture, the weather, and a few things worth a sentence, each on the sky of its own hour. Add the Home replay card to play it with a tap. From 7 PM, the screensaver plays it once first.

items.title: The home talks first
items.line: When you walk up to a screen, the nearest one says one calm line, once.
items.more: For example, "Garage door has been open for 40 minutes" or "Rain starts at about 3 PM. The deck awning is open." It also tells you about a door unlocked at night, a package waiting, the washer being done and low batteries. It learns what you ignore and waits longer next time. Turn it on in the studio under Home moments.

items.title: A new first screen now fills its lower half with what is alive in the house: the door camera, the music that plays, what is open, and scenes
items.line: Room tiles come only when space is left.

items.title: Living cover
items.line: A new music card style.
items.more: The song's cover moves softly, its colors glow behind it, and a thin light along its edge shows how far the song has gone. On a tall card, the cover fills the whole card, like a song video on a phone. Everything holds still when you pause. Swipe the cover to skip a song. It works with every player, not only Spotify. Choose it in the studio under the media card's Style.

fixed: Live camera video now plays on the iPad wall app and in Safari.
